agricultural: broad cultivated land with regular field texture and open farmland layout, distinguishing agricultural from runway by lacking a long straight paved strip, from parkinglot by lacking organized vehicle-row pavement, and from golfcourse by weaker landscaped fairway structure.
airplane: visible aircraft body with wings and tail, compact object-level structure, and clear airplane contours, distinguishing airplane from runway which appears as a long straight paved strip, and from parkinglot which appears as an open paved area without a discrete fuselage.
baseballdiamond: compact sports field with a clear diamond-shaped infield and surrounding outfield, distinguishing baseballdiamond from golfcourse by lacking expansive landscaped fairways, from tenniscourt by lacking small repeated rectangular court markings, and from storagetanks by lacking circular industrial tank geometry.
beach: bright shoreline region with a clear sand-water boundary and open coastal texture, visually distinct from inland land-cover classes by direct coastal water contact.
buildings: large roofed man-made structures with block-like geometry and organized built-up layout, distinguishing buildings from mediumresidential by stronger individual roof mass, from storagetanks by lacking dominant circular tank clusters, and from denseresidential by weaker small-roof repetition and stronger large-structure dominance.
chaparral: dry shrub-covered terrain with coarse natural texture and sparse woody vegetation, distinguishing chaparral from golfcourse by weaker man-made landscaping, from river by lacking a continuous water channel, and from storagetanks by lacking circular industrial structures.
denseresidential: tightly packed residential roofs with very high housing density and minimal spacing, distinguishing denseresidential from mobilehomepark by less uniform trailer-row organization, from tenniscourt by lacking sports-court markings, and from mediumresidential by much closer building intervals.
forest: dense continuous tree canopy with dark green natural texture and little visible built structure, distinguishing forest from mobilehomepark by lacking repeated residential rows, from mediumresidential by lacking organized housing blocks, and from denseresidential by lacking tightly packed roof clusters.
freeway: wide multi-lane transportation corridor with continuous road surface and strong linear flow, distinguishing freeway from overpass by emphasizing extended roadway rather than a local elevated crossing, from runway by lacking aviation-strip context, and from river by paved road texture instead of water appearance.
golfcourse: well-maintained green fairways with landscaped grass regions and designed open-course layout, distinguishing golfcourse from baseballdiamond by lacking a compact diamond infield, from chaparral by stronger man-made landscaping, and from agricultural by less regular cultivated parcel structure.
harbor: waterfront port area with shore-adjacent infrastructure and maritime organization, distinguishing harbor from parkinglot by clear dock-water context, and from storagetanks by stronger shoreline layout and weaker circular-tank dominance.
intersection: road junction region where multiple transportation lines meet, distinguishing intersection from river by road texture instead of water, from runway by emphasizing a compact crossing node rather than a long straight strip, and from denseresidential by road-dominant geometry rather than dense roof clusters.
mediumresidential: moderately spaced residential buildings with visible yards and balanced housing density, distinguishing mediumresidential from denseresidential by larger spacing between houses, from buildings by weaker large-roof dominance, and from forest by visible neighborhood structure rather than continuous tree canopy.
mobilehomepark: repetitive small elongated housing units arranged in orderly rows, distinguishing mobilehomepark from denseresidential by stronger trailer-like regularity, from forest by visible built-unit repetition instead of continuous canopy, and from storagetanks by lacking circular industrial tank clusters.
overpass: elevated crossing transport structure with visible grade separation, distinguishing overpass from freeway by its bridge-like crossing form, from intersection by stronger elevated overlap pattern, and from runway by lacking a long flat aviation strip.
parkinglot: large open paved area with organized parking spaces and vehicle-oriented layout, distinguishing parkinglot from harbor by lacking clear dock-water organization, from agricultural by lacking cultivated field texture, and from buildings by weaker roof dominance and more open paved space.
river: elongated natural watercourse with continuous winding channel and visible banks, distinguishing river from chaparral by clear water appearance, from intersection by lacking road-junction geometry, and from freeway by water-dominant linear structure rather than paved roadway.
runway: long straight paved strip with elongated linear geometry and open surroundings, distinguishing runway from airplane by lacking a discrete aircraft body, from freeway by weaker branching road-network structure, and from agricultural by lacking cultivated field texture.
sparseresidential: widely separated residential houses with large open gaps and low housing density, distinguishing sparseresidential from denseresidential by far lower roof density, from mediumresidential by larger spacing and more open land, and from mobilehomepark by lacking regular trailer-row organization.
storagetanks: clusters of large circular industrial tanks with highly regular round geometry, distinguishing storagetanks from mobilehomepark by lacking elongated housing rows, from buildings by stronger circular-container dominance, and from baseballdiamond by lacking sports-field geometry.
tenniscourt: small rectangular court surfaces with clear line markings and repeated sports-court geometry, distinguishing tenniscourt from denseresidential by lacking dense roof clusters, from baseballdiamond by lacking a diamond-shaped infield, and from storagetanks by lacking circular industrial tank structures.
